finding.claim: The /invoice/<inv_id> route returns any invoice without authentication or an ownership check (IDOR / broken access control). The sibling /my/invoice route enforces customer == g.user['id'], which shows the check is intended.
finding.source: Any unauthenticated or authenticated HTTP client supplies an arbitrary inv_id in the URL path.
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) returns the full invoice record, including the customer field, for any invoice in INVOICES.

trace.note: Route /invoice/<inv_id> is registered with no auth decorator.
INVOICES.get(inv_id) looks up the invoice by the attacker-supplied id, with no ownership comparison.
The full invoice is returned as JSON.

finding.guards_checked: The file has no before_request handler, auth decorator or g.user check on this route. The only ownership check is in get_my_invoice (line 16) and does not apply here. There is no other file in the directory, so no middleware could apply. Invoice IDs may be guessable or enumerable, which makes exploitation easier.

verdict.reason: invoices.py:7-10 registers /invoice/<inv_id> with no auth decorator, before_request hook or ownership check and returns jsonify(inv) for any ID, unlike the sibling check at invoices.py:16.
